findings.evidence: Each backbone carries only features that belong to it: the pSStarget circle in A, and the linearized/ligated cassette constructs in B and D; the excised ccdB fragment and the incoming spacer are drawn as separate detached backbones.
The single-stranded Fwd and Rev oligonucleotides in panel C are each drawn as a single line (with base ticks), while annealed and plasmid DNA is drawn with two lines.
All feature glyphs are anchored on their backbone: arrows sit on the circular backbone in A, and the P arrow, ccdB/spacer and sgRNA boxes sit inline on the double-stranded line in B and D.

Promoters are drawn with the arrow form used for CDSs: p32, pCas, pTc and pEPS in panel A are green block arrows identical in shape to the purple CDS arrows (repE, cat, cas9, TcR), and the 'P' promoter in panels B and D is the same block-arrow form. The glyph asserts a CDS role the feature does not have.
BsaI is a generic labeled cloud shape and the ligation complexes in D are generic unlabeled blobs; no glyph asserts an incorrect molecular species type.
The BsaI clouds in B and the pink ligation blobs in D contact only the DNA they act on (cleavage sites and ligation junctions), which is an interaction.
No two interaction edges intersect anywhere in the figure.
The enzyme-action arrows (BsaI to cut site, fragment transfer) use plain arrowheads as generic process indicators, reinforced by the scissors icon; no arrow asserts an incorrect interaction type.
No multi-headed edges appear in the figure.
No interaction node glyphs are used; interactions are drawn as simple edges.
No edge terminates on the head or tail of another edge.
The rectangles around B, C and D are panel frames, not subsystem boundary glyphs; no subsystems are depicted.
No interface rectangles are used.
Double-stranded constructs in B, C and D use a double-lined ladder backbone while the single-stranded oligos in C use a single line.
Panel A uses a closed loop to indicate the cyclic plasmid; backbones in B, C and D are horizontal.
The circular backbone in panel A conveys the plasmid, and omitted material in B and D is explicitly marked at the break in the backbone.
Every backbone drawn carries at least one feature glyph.
Feature glyphs are centered on and aligned to the backbone line in all panels.
Reverse-orientation features in panel A (repE, repD, copS, cat, TcR, ccdB, ccdA) are consistently shown as 180-degree-rotated arrows pointing counterclockwise, not mirrored-only.
Forward features point clockwise/left-to-right (cas9, sgRNA cassette, P) and reverse-complement features point the opposite way consistently.
Adjacent glyphs such as cat/p32/pCas and p15A ori/pTc abut but their drawn shapes do not overlap.

In panel A the subparts of the sgRNA cassette (sgRNA handle, ccdB, ccdA fragment, pEPS) lie within the cassette's coordinates, per the caption, yet they are drawn on a separate inner concentric track that does not overlap the cyan sgRNA cassette glyph.

Promoters use the CDS block-arrow form rather than the promoter glyph (p32, pCas, pTc, pEPS, and 'P' in B/D), the p15A origin is a plain box rather than the origin-of-replication glyph, and omitted material in B and D is shown with a double-slash line break, which is explicitly compliant but not best practice.
BsaI and the ligation complexes are drawn as irregular lumpy cloud blobs rather than the recommended macromolecule glyph (or its degenerate oval form).

In panel D the pink ligation blobs overlap the construct well beyond the ligation junctions — the left blob covers the green promoter arrow — and no feature glyph marks the overlap location as the site of the interaction.
No interaction edges cross one another in any panel.
Enzymatic cleavage by BsaI and ligation are indicated with plain generic arrowheads plus a scissors clip-art icon rather than the recommended specific interaction glyphs.
No interaction nodes are drawn.
No multi-head or multi-tail arrows are present.
No subsystem boundaries are drawn; the panel borders are figure layout frames.
Names sit inside their glyphs or are attached by short leader lines (repD, copS, p32, sgRNA handle, ccdB, ccdA, pEPS, BsaI site coordinates), keeping each label visually tied to its glyph.

figures.rationale: Panel A is a full plasmid map of pSStarget showing promoters, CDSs, an origin, and the sgRNA cassette laid out on a circular backbone, and panels B and D show the composition of the sgRNA expression cassette on double-stranded backbones; communicating the construct's design is a primary purpose of the figure.

findings.evidence: Plasmid features (Cas9, sgRNA, Cm^R) are all on the pSStarget circle; repair-template segments and chromosomal features are drawn on their own separate backbones.
No single-stranded nucleic acid construct backbone is depicted; all constructs shown are double-stranded DNA (plasmid, RT, chromosome).
Cas9/Cm^R arrows and the sgRNA box are anchored on the plasmid circle; the target gene box and colored region bars sit directly on the linear chromosome/RT backbones.

Cas9 and Cm^R use the accepted arrow CDS form; target gene, sgRNA and homology/modified regions are generic labeled rectangles/bars, which the panel accepts as compliant. No glyph asserts an incorrect role.
Cas9 is a novel labeled blue blob with bound sgRNA; a generic labeled species shape asserting no incorrect type.

The only species–construct contact is the Cas9/sgRNA complex overlapping the target site in panel C (right), which is exactly the interaction being depicted; the panel C (left) Cas9 in the legend touches no construct.
No interaction edge glyphs are present; the crossing thin lines in panel B are homology-correspondence guides in a recombination illustration and the grey block arrows are workflow-flow arrows.
No interaction edges are drawn; cleavage is conveyed pictorially by scissors rather than by an interaction glyph.
No multi-headed edges appear in the figure.
No interaction nodes are used.
No edges connect to the head or tail of another edge; the branch arrows below the cell split from a plain line, not from an interaction edge.
The light rectangles in panel B are magnification callouts of the chromosome, not subsystem boundaries; the cell outline in panel A contains no feature or species glyphs crossing it.
No interface rectangles are used.
Only double-stranded constructs are drawn as constructs; no mixed single/double-stranded depiction requiring the distinction.
pSStarget uses a closed loop appropriate for a circular plasmid; the RT and chromosomal backbones are horizontal.

The chromosomal locus in panels B and C is drawn as a plain bar/line that simply terminates: no locus glyph is used and no omitted-detail glyph marks the surrounding genomic context that is not shown.
Every backbone carries at least one region/feature glyph (plasmid: Cas9, sgRNA, Cm^R; RT and chromosome: homology arm and modified-region bars, target gene box).
Feature glyphs are centered on and aligned to their backbones on both the circular plasmid and the linear constructs.
No reverse-complement features are indicated anywhere in the figure.
The only direction-bearing glyphs, the Cas9 and Cm^R arrows, both run clockwise on the plasmid, a consistent 5'-to-3' presentation.
The target gene box only abuts the flanking region bars at their shared junctions; under the bounding-box flexibility exception this is acceptable.
No features with genuinely overlapping locations are depicted.

The target gene is a plain green rectangle rather than a CDS glyph, the sgRNA cassette is an unlabeled small blue box, and the homology arm/modified region are plain colored bars instead of the most specific applicable glyphs.
Cas9 is drawn as a novel but self-consistent protein/RNP shape with its bound sgRNA, acceptable as a novel more-specific glyph.

In panel C (right) the Cas9 complex overlaps the target gene box, but the sgRNA target site is marked only by an asterisk with an off-figure footnote rather than by a feature glyph appropriate to the binding/cleavage interaction, and the blob spills beyond the gene glyph.
No interaction edges are present; the crossing lines in panel B are recombination correspondence guides.
No interaction edges are drawn.
No interaction nodes are drawn.
No multi-head or multi-tail arrows appear.
No subsystem boundaries are used; the rectangles are zoom callouts and the cell is an illustrative outline.
